name: RF Attacks and BIC Safety
summary: Use an RF version, see its fallback, then make a risky one safe.
description: Use an RF version, see its fallback, then make a risky one safe.

pages.title: RF Versions
pages.text: Many Specials have a beefed-up RF version, usually done with C - better damage, priority, or invulnerability. The price: half the gauge at Red, a quarter at Light Blue. Ask for one without enough RF and the B version comes out instead.

pages.title: BIC Safety
pages.text: At Light Blue RF, an RF Attack costs only a quarter of the full gauge. And unlike Red IC, BIC can cancel an RF Attack, spending the remaining Blue gauge. That's how you make a risky RF Special safe when it's guarded - even an invincible pressure-escape attack, called a {term:reversal}. And if it hits instead? The same BIC rolls straight into a combo.

feedback.success: That's the RF version - C plus the prepared Red gauge paid for it.
feedback.failure: Your Red gauge is ready - just input 623C cleanly.

tasks.label: Try {input:623C} with an EMPTY RF Gauge - see what comes out

feedback.success: See that? RF was empty, so the same C input fell back to the B version.
feedback.failure: Once the RF version finishes, throw out 623C again with the gauge empty.

tasks.label: Blocked {input:623C}? Blue IC in the air, then stay safe
tasks.prompt: The dummy blocks your {input:623C} - and the move leaves you AIRBORNE. Spend the Blue gauge on an air IC ({input:22C}) to cut the recovery, then guard the answer - or double-jump {dir:7} away.

feedback.success: BIC canceled the blocked RF attack in time to guard or double-jump away from the answer.
feedback.failure: Use 623C at Light Blue RF, BIC it with 22C as it is blocked, then guard or double-jump back instead of pressing another attack.

cue.text: Blocked! Air BIC - then stay safe.
